title: Uniform provisions concerning the approval of motor vehicles having at least four wheels with regard to their sound emissions (Sound of M and N categories of vehicles)
scope_summary: UN R51 approves vehicle types with regard to the sound they emit, using test procedures meant to reproduce sound levels during normal urban driving. It applies to motor vehicles of categories M and N, with Additional Sound Emission Provisions (ASEP, Annex 7) for M1 and N1 and an evaluation-only Real Driving ASEP (Annex 9).
scope_quote: This Regulation contains provisions on the sound emitted by motor vehicles and applies to vehicles of categories M and N. The specifications in this Regulation are intended to reproduce the sound levels which are generated by vehicles during normal driving in urban traffic. This Regulation provides, as well, Additional Sound Emission Provisions for vehicles of categories M1 and N1 referring to driving conditions with extreme accelerations in an extended speed range representative for urban and suburban traffic.
applies_to_components: Sound reduction system / silencing system (intake and exhaust silencing components)
Exhaust silencing systems and components containing sound absorbing fibrous materials
Exhaust silencing system with variable geometry (RD-ASEP, Annex 9)
Engine / power source (combustion engine, electric motor, hybrid drive train) as sound source
Transmission / gear ratios, kickdown and downshift-prevention control
Compressed air equipment (compressed air noise, Annex 5)
Tyres (tyre rolling sound and temperature correction, Annex 3 Appendix 2)
relation_to_other_regulations: Refers to UN Regulation No. 85 for determining maximum net power and rated engine speed (paragraphs 5.2 and 5.3)
Refers to UN GTR No. 21 for system power of hybrid / multi-converter electric vehicles
Refers to the Consolidated Resolution on the Construction of Vehicles (R.E.3) for vehicle category definitions and the R-point
Refers to ISO 612-1978 for vehicle length and width and ISO 10844 for the test track surface
Paragraph 4.3 notes components may carry approval numbers as components of replacement silencing systems (approved separately under another regulation)
Conformity of production follows the general procedures of the 1958 Agreement (Schedule 1)

applicability_hints: The intake system is part of the 'silencing system' (engine, intake and exhaust sound), so air intake silencers/resonators are covered, while exhaust manifolds, catalysts and after-treatment devices are excluded (they belong to the engine)
Any silencer or silencer component using sound absorbing fibrous material triggers paragraph 6.3 and Annex 4 (design family, conditioning tests)
Electric motors and hydraulic power sources count as 'engine'; BEV, FCEV and HEV are within scope and the electric motor type is a vehicle type criterion
Changes to engine compartment shape, materials or soundproofing (e.g. encapsulation, insulation panels) can constitute a change of vehicle type

Exhaust flaps/valves or other variable-geometry silencing systems and driver-selectable sound-affecting modes (drive modes, sound settings) are addressed by ASEP/RD-ASEP and anti-manipulation provisions
Engine and transmission control software (engine mappings, kickdown, downshift prevention, locked gear ratio) affects test conditions and anti-manipulation compliance
Vehicles equipped with compressed air systems (e.g. air brakes, air suspension) are subject to compressed air noise measurement per Annex 5
Tyres fitted influence the pass-by result and tyre rolling sound correction (Annex 3 Appendices 2 and 3)

Components of the sound reduction system (excluding fixing hardware and piping) must bear manufacturer trade name and trade description markings; aftermarket replacement silencing systems relate to this regulation via marking and approval numbers
